Albert Einstein did **not** win the Nobel Prize for his theory of relativity. 

He was awarded the **1921 Nobel Prize in Physics** (which was actually announced and presented to him in November 1922) specifically for his **services to Theoretical Physics, and especially for his discovery of the law of the photoelectric effect**. 

While his theories of relativity (special and general) are his most famous contributions to science, the Nobel Committee at the time considered them still too controversial and lacking absolute definitive proof, so they chose to honor him for his work on the photoelectric effect instead.
